title: Why the Série B Standings Are Hot Right Now
seoTitle: Série B Standings: Promotion & Relegation Battle Heats Up
subtitle: Analysis of the Last Eight Games and Promotion/Relegation Chances
excerpt: As Série B nears its end, the race for promotion and the battle against relegation intensify. Discover which teams face the toughest schedules and how it impacts their.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
With only eight rounds remaining, the battle for promotion to Série A and the fight to avoid relegation have intensified even further. The scenario has changed because the standings now determine not only two direct spots, but also two playoff matchups between clubs finishing between third and sixth place.

What Defines the Difficulty of the Schedule

The ge portal calculated a difficulty index by summing the accumulated points of the opponents each team will still face until the end of the competition. The higher the sum, the more complicated the schedule.

Vila Nova Faces the Toughest Schedule

The isolated leader, Vila Nova, accumulates the highest degree of difficulty, assessed at 367 points. In upcoming clashes, the club from Formiga faces Juventude, Fortaleza, Novorizontino, and Criciúma – who occupy, respectively, second, third, fourth, and fifth places in the standings. No opponent is in the relegation zone, but all are direct competitors for promotion.

Sport Emerges as the Second Most Challenged

Right behind Vila Nova, Sport has an index of 360 points, being the only club that comes close to the leader in terms of difficulty. The red-and-black team still has games against teams that could change their position in the G6.

Criciúma Has the Most Favorable Schedule Among the Ten Analyzed

At the other end of the table, Criciúma presents the lowest difficulty, with 285 points. The club faces opponents who, so far, have accumulated fewer points than the others, which could be a differential in the race for promotion.

How the New Playoff Format Alters the Competition

In addition to the two direct spots, clubs finishing between third and sixth place will compete in two home-and-away playoff matches: 3rd vs 6th and 4th vs 5th. Teams finishing third and fourth have the advantage of playing the decisive leg at home, increasing the importance of every point in the final rounds.

Relegation Risk: The Case of Ceará

At the bottom of the table, Ceará leads the relegation zone with 36 points and needs nine points to escape the specter of relegation. Their next opponents are Botafogo-SP, Avaí, and Londrina, all with distinct situations in the fight against the drop.

With the combination of tough schedules, the new playoff system, and the closeness between the top teams, the Série B standings have become the most talked-about topic among fans following the final stretch of the championship.

With information from ge, O POVO, UOL.
